## Project Overview

**RailActive** investigates the potential to repurpose High Speed Two (HS2) construction assets—including haul roads, access tracks, and maintenance strips—into a high-quality, segregated, multi-user active travel spine.

The corridor stretches from London Euston / Old Oak Common through the Colne Valley, Chilterns, and rural Midlands into Birmingham Curzon Street, with wider strategic feeder links extending toward the North West ({{< var corridor_total_km >}} km total network in {{< var corridor_version >}}).

Key project aims include:

- **Infrastructure Repurposing**: Identifying where temporary construction access roads and haul tracks can be permanently retained for cycling, walking, and wheeling.
- **Severance Reduction**: Overcoming historical and modern transport barriers (motorways, rail corridors, rivers) to reconnect fragmented rural communities.
- **Empirical Demand Modeling**: Integrating commute, school, and leisure trip generators to estimate uptake.
- **Economic Benefits Appraisal**: Applying the Department for Transport's (DfT) Active Mode Appraisal Toolkit (AMAT) and ATE's *Active Mode Benefits: Theoretical Framework* [@nellthorp2026] to quantify decongestion, health mortality, workplace absenteeism, and journey ambience benefits.

## System Architecture

The RailActive analytical and web mapping platform combines R spatial pipelines with a serverless web frontend:

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    Ingest["Data Ingestion & Spatial Backend<br/>R targets (sf, dodgr, osmextract) + Python<br/>OSM, NCN, OS OpenRoads, HS2 Haul Routes, STATS19, Census & NTS"]
    Artifacts["Analytical Artifacts<br/>GeoJSON / GeoParquet • DuckDB • PMTiles vector tiles"]
    Frontend["Frontend Web Application<br/>Svelte 5 (Runes) + MapLibre GL + DuckDB-WASM<br/>Client-side SQL & interactive map without a backend server"]
    Ingest --> Artifacts --> Frontend
```

## Documentation Guide

- [**Methodology**](methods.qmd): Empirical trip purpose weighting (NTS & Active Lives Survey), network connectivity, and AMAT economic valuation.
- [**Uptake Modelling Decision Brief (Ox–Ux)**](uptake_case_study.qmd): Concise first-principles uptake method, Oxfordshire–Uxbridge case study, worked example, and eight choices for economic appraisal.
- [**Uptake Modelling Technical Appendix**](uptake_appendix.qmd): Prototype audit, full PCT/Bass equations, supplementary diagnostics, and standardised 4-table demand-to-AMAT schema.
- [**Data Dictionary**](data_dictionary.qmd): Formal schema and variable definitions for active datasets (corridor geometries, client GPX tracks, OS OpenRoads, STATS19 safety, OSM, and Sustrans NCN).
- [**Data Inventory**](data_inventory.qmd): Catalog of primary project assets, John Grimshaw CBE feasibility studies, SAR retention proposals, and spatial archives.
